meta.title: Mechacut — same request, same bytes
meta.desc: Deterministic transforms for AI agents: 184 tools, three tiers, machine payments. No signup, no key, no storage.
hero.plain: In plain words: Mechacut does the exact counting for AI assistants. Splitting a bill, a due date, a currency, a file — the assistant asks, Mechacut answers, and the answer is always the same. And when one assistant learns something new, every assistant gets it the same day.
dev.intro: Everything above was true. Below is how: the full API, the tool catalogue, the schemas, the benchmarks, the pricing. No prose — references.
hero.why: Why determinism? Because a right answer that changes on every run is not an answer — it is a dice roll. A machine that returns the same bytes for the same question makes agents auditable: every response carries its checksum, every error names the offending field, and what you test in the morning is what you ship at night.
demo.title: ASK THE BENCH — live, keyless, same bytes every run
demo.hint: press Run — the answer below comes from the real endpoint, not a screenshot
demo.err: network hiccup — the endpoint still answers: POST /api/v1/num/round
hero3: Competence is not learned. It is served.
lede: A suite of 188 deterministic transforms for AI agents — 152 free forever, 26 free under 32 KB then pay-per-call, 10 machine-payable — plus 9 one-call recipes, free. The model stops guessing what a checksum can prove.
bundles.creed: A model computes. A server knows.
cat.search: search a tool or your problem…
bundles.intro: Same request, same bytes — every response carries its own sha256. Install one pack, or read the whole manifest in one request and let GET /route pick.
tiers.intro: Agents do not read pricing pages — so the price is in the protocol: a free route answers keyless, a capped route answers free under 32 KB, anything else gets an honest 402 with an x402 USDC-on-Base challenge, settled by a facilitator. Between a server and a robot, only prices and receipts exist.
bench.h2: Benchmarks, or what we looked for:
bench.creed: The wall is FORM, not size — and we priced the door.
bench9.intro: One deliberately vague French sentence, six required fields — money sorted to 2 decimals, percents, unique dates, URL, email, total. Expectations hand-computed before any run. The server builds the card (/intent/card); the model relays one line and the answer never passes through it.
bench9.foot: The 0.5B row reproduced on an independent second pass. Three identical live calls returned one sha256. The autonomous variant (the model picks the tool itself, no card played by the harness) also scores 6/6. Seeds, scripts, failures: bench/results_v9.jsonl.
bench10.intro: Eighteen tasks with ONE right answer each — GS1 check digits, a SHA-256, chained discounts, a money column that proves its own decimal comma. Two free LOCAL models, no API spend: the harness asserts every route it calls is free. Golds were computed from the published specs before any model ran.
bench10.foot: Naked failures reproduce on an independent second pass, 18/18 verdicts identical — at temp 0 a retry never converges, it repeats. Raw runs: bench/results_v10.jsonl, method: bench/FINDINGS-V10.md.
bench.v23.sum: A 1.7B trained for agents solved 7/7 chains naked for $0.0018 — our wall was TRAINING, not size; and the lock refused 2 right answers over their names.
bench.v23.intro: The cross-family replication: the same 20 seeded problems, the same arms as v20, one model of another lineage (LFM3-1.7B, tri-hybrid, post-trained for tool calls). Nude 20/20, relayed 18/20, locked 18/20. Nothing here refutes v19: answering right once is not answering with the same byte thirty days running.
bench.v23.foot: Raw: bench/results_v23_lfm3.jsonl · method: bench/FINDINGS-V23.md · $ at frozen per-token prices.
bench.v20.sum: The wall is AIM: llama 8B went 10→13/20 with a target lock; the 7B signed its first 20/20.
bench.v20.intro: The promise of v17, measured: the answer must name the quantity it returns. Nude, the 8B computed right and answered beside it — 3 of its misses carried another quantity of the chain; the lock converted 3. 120 cells, and the naked arm replays v15 exactly (10/19/11).
bench.g1: What they miss is executing, not thinking
bench.g2: The wall is a SHAPE — and shapes are a training target
bench.g3: Nobody says "I'm not sure" — paying more doesn't dodge the shape
bench.g4: Reading is the ceiling no tool breaks
bench.g5: The real regime: thirty days of the same job
bench.v11.sum: Fifteen hostile tasks: the 7B goes 3/15 to 13/15 relayed; the 8B 0/15 to 13/15.
bench.f5.sum: 20/56 chain attempts with the fiche — criterion ≥19 PASSED; 34 repaired by a named refusal; the 7B alone 12/14.
bench.v13.sum: The negative result, published first: on real GSM8K the relay card falls to 0/20 for the 0.5B — asking the model for the decomposition still leaves it doing the decomposition.
bench.v14.sum: Strict skill: 3/80 protocol breaks — the class the form can guarantee — while reading stays free.
bench.v22.sum: Three frontier models answer 10/21 naked — one at 7/7, another at 0/7. Through the frozen fiche: 19/21. Paying more doesn't change the shape.
bench.v22b.sum: Five passes at agent temperature: 70/70 right — the SAME program twice: 0/14. The server: 1 sha per problem.
bench.v24.sum: Thirty days of the same CSV with a model that CAN do chains: 25/30 days of empty answers after 8,192 reasoning tokens, 4 right, billed $0.0493. The machine: 30/30 at $0.00.
bench.f7.sum: EN/PT copies of the seven chains: 27/56 — criterion ≥19 passed; 17 of them won by the named refusal. PT copy at 4/7 vs FR's 0/7 on the 0.5B: the reading ceiling belongs to model × language × form.
bench.v24.foot: Raw: bench/results_v24_lfm3_30days.jsonl · the amendment lives in git history (run24 amendé)
bench.v19.sum: 0/120 attempts right for the models — machine: 30/30 days on one identical hash; 21 different outputs from one model in 30 days.
bench.v19.intro: The same dirty CSV cleaned 30 days in a row. Six-rule spec, a gold file written BY HAND before the harness, a retry arm that only ever sees its own format — never the answer. Temperature 0.7: the real regime of agents, disclosed.
bench.v19.foot: Raw: bench/results_v19_csv_bill.jsonl · method + dollars: bench/FINDINGS-V19.md · replay: python bench/run19.py
bench.v17.sum: Retry ×5 on a systematic miss: 0/14 chains fixed — the same mistake, ×5 the price.
bench.v17.intro: Three arms, the same 20 fresh problems, every token counted: answer naked, retry five times, or hand the calculation to the server. Cells: 80.
bench.v17.foot: Raw: bench/results_v17_tokens.jsonl · bench/FINDINGS-V17.md · replay: python bench/run17.py
bench.v16.sum: 63 wrong answers in 80 runs — 'I'm not sure' said 0 times.
bench.v16.intro: Everyday word problems, freshly generated, each model asked to mark its own confidence honestly. They failed the same way every time: confidently.
bench.v16.foot: Raw: bench/results_v16_calibration.jsonl · bench/FINDINGS-V16.md · generator: bench/gen16.py (seeded, double oracle).
bench.v15.sum: The wall is a SHAPE: 0/56 chain attempts solved naked or retried — 11/28 by the best server arm.
bench.v15.intro: The full matrix: 5 transports × 4 free models × 20 seeded problems (400 cells), hypotheses committed BEFORE the first run, failed predictions published first.
bench.v15.foot: Raw: bench/results_v15_matrix.jsonl · bench/FINDINGS-V15.md · replay: python bench/run15.py && python bench/score15.py
bench.v12.sum: 0/10 alone → 9/10 with one relay call. The zero becomes the hero.
bench.v10.sum: One right answer each: 3/18 alone → 18/18 relayed — at $0, audited by the harness itself.
bench.v9.sum: One vague sentence, six keys: 0/6 → 6/6 with the intake card.
bench.v6.sum: The first matrix — naked vs relay. Every row, harness and failure: bench/FINDINGS.md.
bench12.intro: Ten exact calculations (7834×9217, 0.1+0.2, chained percentages…) × four FREE local models × three arms: answering naked, writing Python, or relaying one expression to math/calc. Scores shown; the code arm's answers are float, the relay's are exact — same table, different physics.
bench12.foot: The 8B fails RELAY on protocol babble, not math — which is why the intake card writes the line for it. The 0.5B invented 89000098 naked and posts 9/10 relayed at 0.2 s median. Raw: bench/results_v12.jsonl, method: bench/FINDINGS-V12.md.
bench.intro: A frozen task (seed 20261120): dirty CSV + broken JSON + URL list → one canonical YAML, expected answer pinned by sha256. Same weak local model (Qwen 2.5, temperature 0), one arm alone, one arm driving Mechacut. We publish the failures too — the 0.5B fails both arms, and a capability ceiling is a result.
bench.foot: The 7B goes from 0 % to 100 % in a single pipeline call. Every run, every token, is in bench/results.jsonl.
market.creed: The big houses converged on the same sentence — only the delivery differs.
build.intro: You have a free small model on your machine. Here are three things to make it do — the quoted lines are what you say to your agent, the answers below are what the server really returned. No account, no card, no prayer.
build.r1.name: The tax-ID gate
build.r1.say: “Is my client’s VAT number FR40303265045 valid for the invoice?”
build.r1.got: { "valid": true, "algorithm": "EU VAT check-digit rule for FR (published)" }
build.r1.why: Alone, a 0.5B model computes check digits — and gets them wrong. Here the digits decide, so the invoice does not die at the accountant’s. Every country’s flavour lives on its own page: CNPJ for Brazil, SIREN and TVA for France.
build.r2.name: The leak guard
build.r2.say: “Scan this log before I paste it into a chatbot.”
build.r2.why: The scan answers with positions, never the value; the mask never returns the key. The secret came here for safekeeping — it stays safe from us too.
build.r3.name: The incident relay
build.r3.say: “relève les montants et dates de cette note d’incident” — said in French, to a 0.5B.
build.r3.why: That is bench v9 verbatim: same task, same model, one relay line. Every run is in bench/results_v9.jsonl — replay it yourself.
build.connect: Or skip the story and wire it now: paste this ONE line into ANY agent, even the smallest — it becomes the full manual:
everyday.open: Expand the proofs — real server outputs, no mockups.
everyday.intro: No code, no jargon. Twenty-eight things a person asks an agent on a Tuesday — every answer below is real server output, not a mockup.
everyday.e1.name: Guest Wi-Fi, one scan
everyday.e1.say: “Turn our Wi-Fi into a QR so guests stop asking the password.”
everyday.e2.name: The check, in words
everyday.e2.say: “Write $1,234.56 in words for the check — the bank rejects typos.”
everyday.e3.name: IBAN before the wire
everyday.e3.say: “Did I copy this IBAN right? A bounced wire costs $45.”
everyday.e4.name: Recipe to printable page
everyday.e4.say: “Make my recipe notes a clean page — I want a PDF for the fridge.”
everyday.e5.name: Counting the days
everyday.e6.name: Sale math the register will not do
everyday.e6.say: “Minus 30 %, then another 20 % — that is 50 % off, right?” It is 44 %.
everyday.e7.name: A third of the cake, nothing rounded in the dark
everyday.e7.say: “This 6-serving cake, I want it for 2 — 400 g flour, 5 eggs?” 400 × 1/3 = 133 1/3 g exact, 135 g to weigh. The eggs are stated, not guessed.
everyday.e8.name: Every other Tuesday, on the dot
everyday.e8.say: “Book club every other Tuesday at 7 — the next four dates?” Nov 3, 17, Dec 1, 15: every two weeks means SKIPPING the weeks between — and the skipped weeks are named, not guessed.
everyday.e9.name: One foot, three right answers
everyday.e9.say: “EU 42 2/3 or 42.5 — which one am I?” Both charts round: the millimetre is exact, the half-size and third-size candidates are all printed, and the drift between systems is a stated number. Never one confident size.
everyday.e10.name: Delayed flight — who owes me what
everyday.e10.say: “My flight landed 3 h 20 late — what am I actually owed?” The FLIGHT DATE picks the rule: before 2027-10-23 the old EC261 + case-law; on or after it, the new codified ‘EXCEEDING three hours’ table. Same facts either side of that line can pay differently. € or £, with the claim deadline as a real date.
everyday.e11.name: Will my bag pass the gate
everyday.e11.say: “My bag is 40×18×12, flight in November 2027 — free under the seat? The FLIGHT DATE decides: the 2027 law caps the under-seat item at 40×30×15, nothing before it. Rotation counts — faces sorted, never the order you typed.
everyday.e12.name: The two tariffs, one honest number
everyday.e12.say: “Plan A is cheaper per kWh, plan B is cheaper per month — when does A really win?” The crossover is (fixed gap × days) ÷ (rate gap) — and the exact fraction, not the web's rounded intermediate: 4,623⅓ kWh where the article says “about 4,623”. “Never” is also an answer, named, when one plan wins on both parts.
everyday.e13.name: What a point is really worth
everyday.e13.say: “29,000 points for a $438 flight minus $5.60 taxes — how much is a point, really?” cpp = (cash − taxes) ÷ points × 100: the printed 1.49 hides the exact 1081/725 = 1.491034…, subtracted BEFORE dividing. And the floor that says take-it-or-pay-cash is yours, never a stale table.
everyday.e14.name: The billed weight, both chains printed
everyday.e14.say: “Two carriers bill 6 kg and 5 kg for my 40×30×25 box — who is wrong?” Neither: 30 000 cm³ ÷ 5 000 = 6 exactly, ÷ 6 000 = 5 exactly — two divisors, one honest chain, each step named. And carrier tables ROT (USPS moved 166 → 139 in July 2026), so the divisor stays YOUR argument — never our memory.
everyday.e15.name: The BOGO sign says 50 % — the bill does not
everyday.e15.say: “Buy one, get the second 50 % off — a $60 and a $40 hoodie, am I at −50, −25?” Neither: the % hits the CHEAPER item (published retail rule), so the pair is 80 of 100 = −20 %. Equal prices would be −25 %, BOGO free −50 %, and a −30 coupon on top gives −47.5, never 55 — percentages multiply.
everyday.e16.name: The 500 g pack became 400 g — at the same price
everyday.e16.say: “−20 % on the package?” Not the same number as the shelf: losing 1/5 of the product costs +1/4 per unit (20 % vs 25 % — two denominators, 500 and 400). “2 for $7” of 15 oz jars vs one 24 oz at $3.99? The eye says promo, the exact fraction says the single jar wins — the bundle pays 40.3509 % more per ounce. And “1 lb 4 oz” IS 20 oz: the coupon was right, the cashier wasn’t.
everyday.e17.name: Thanksgiving turkey: the freezer clock AND the leftover window
everyday.e17.say: Two clocks, one turkey. Fridge math (8 November 2026 calendars disagree on the same USDA table): in by = oven − longest tail, not before = − 1-2 day rest; hours are ARGUMENTS, never the wall clock; done = 165 °F at the probe. Leftovers: 'eat by Monday 30 November' (NBC) vs 'three days, 72 hours is the optimum' (ky3); FSIS contradicts itself on the freezer (2-6 vs 3-4 months) — the tool returns the UNION, two dated anchors, and 2 h STRICT since cooked_at (2 h flat passes, 2 h 01 discards), day 4 = LAST_DAY, quality named quality.
everyday.e18.name: Three dishes want the oven — the countdown, every conflict named
everyday.e18.say: Eight 2026 timelines publish the same dinner with rests of 20 to 60 minutes, 325 or 350 °F — and nobody counts the preheat that eats 45 minutes. Scheduled BACKWARDS from your serve_at (an argument, never the wall clock): one oven, one dish, rests outside; a dish entering the instant the previous leaves at another setting is a named conflict; a bare 180 without a unit is refused; rest beyond 2 h hits the FSIS danger zone — same rule as the leftovers window.
everyday.e19.name: Christmas ship-by dates — ≥2 sources per row, the outlier NAMED
everyday.e19.say: Six holiday tables published Nov 13–21, 2026 disagree: one syndicate prints FedEx Saver, 2Day and Overnight a full day later — silently, because its target is Dec 25, not Dec 24. Keeps only rows where ≥2 sources agree, names the dissenter WITH its reason, derives every weekday from the calendar the press itself cites, refuses UPS Ground (zone-dependent — no single date exists) and never extrapolates a year. as_of is an argument: « how many days are left » is arithmetic, not a clock. The window dies Dec 23.
everyday.e20.name: Holiday RETURN deadlines — ≥2 sources, provenance class on every row
everyday.e20.say: The shared January-31 headline is a lie of omission: Target's purchase window closes Dec 24, Best Buy's member rule splits at Dec 4, and parcelmonitor republished last year's dates shifted by one as a 'likely pattern' while Seller Central had published the 2026 text verbatim. Keeps only rows with two concordant sources, carries provenance (published|press), names the Day-1 counting convention, refuses single-source retailers WITH the candidate fact, never lets 'whichever is later' be a guess: delivery date is an argument.
everyday.e21.name: Is that crossed-out price LEGAL — the Omnibus 30-day rule, audited from your own history
everyday.e21.say: Legal reference: the LOWEST price of the previous 30 days (dir. 2019/2161 art. 6a) — a weekend promo LOWERS the reference even if the price rises after (CJEU C-330/23). 100 → 80 → 100 → 70 = 12.5 %, not 30 %. Commission sweep, March 2026: 30 % of 314 shops get it wrong; Spain fined up to 350,000 EUR. History in, reference and true % out — never fetches a price.
everyday.e22.name: Price DROPPED after you paid — who owes the difference, by when, in which money
everyday.e22.say: You bought at 100, the shop now shows 80. No law forces a refund — but the shops' own published guarantees do, and those windows are DATES: Target Dec 24, Best Buy Jan 15, Costco 30 days, Fnac-Darty the campaign itself (gift card, not cash), Amazon nothing at all. Paste purchase + drop dates and both prices — the machine returns the verdict, the claim deadline, the amount and the refund mode, with the source class on every row. It never fetches a price.
everyday.e23.name: The gift broke AFTER the return window — what does the LAW still owe you, to the day
everyday.e23.say: Christmas gift, delivered Dec 25, dies Jan 16: the shop's goodwill window closed Jan 15 and the press stops answering here. The statute doesn't. France: conformity 2 years from DELIVERY, hidden defects 2 from DISCOVERY under a 20-year cap — three anchors under one word. UK: 30 days to reject, six months of reversed burden (a PROOF rule, not a deadline), six years to sue — five in Scotland. Every answer is dated from your one input; official page contradicting itself (refurbished, 24 vs 12): BOTH dates travel named. US and AU refused by name: no federal countable window; 'reasonable time' is not a date.
everyday.e24.name: Can I shred this folder? — the UK drawer hides FOUR clocks
everyday.e24.say: “Six years” is ONE phrase for four dates: VAT invoices count from the date ON THE DOCUMENT (even a paper for a future event — the HMRC manual says so), a limited company from the END of the financial year, s.388 THREE years if private / SIX if a plc from the date MADE, Self Assessment five years from a 31-Jan deadline on no document. Official example replayed: a 2022-23 return sent by 31 January 2024 keeps the paper until 31 January 2029, shred from 1 February. The “or longer if” cases (late return, open compliance check) come back BLOCKED, reason published — no invented date; when two rules touch one paper, the LONGER governs (CH15400, replayed after its 2026-11-23 update).
everyday.e25.name: The gift voucher that 'expired' may be legally alive — Ireland counts from the BUY
everyday.e25.say: Ireland (Consumer Protection (Gift Vouchers) Act 2019, text replayed): a printed expiry shorter than FIVE YEARS from purchase is not voided — DEEMED REPLACED by five years; the legal date OVERRIDES the paper (66B(1)(b)+(c)). JD Sports shape: one-year vouchers, ~€250,000 refunded in July after the CCPC 20-Nov call-in. A Christmas gift-card starts no clock — the anchor is the contract date, the RECIPIENT holds every right (66B(10)). A leftover of €1 or more is owed — and the €1.00 boundary conflict ships named: the Act says 'or more', the CCPC FAQ 'more than'. France: NO statutory minimum; the printed date is contractual; the '30 years' rumour is real-property prescription, refused by name.
everyday.e26.name: Sale dates: three tables — two formulas, zero in Luxembourg
everyday.e26.say: Three replayed calendars. France (arrete 27-May-2019): winter = 2nd Wednesday of January 8h, advanced when the 2nd falls after the 12th (2027: 6 Jan — the 9-Feb site lost the clause); summer = last Wed of June, penultimate when the last falls after the 28th (2027: 23 June); four weeks, start day counted; seven derogations verbatim (Moselle alone 26 June 2021; winter 2021 SIX WEEKS; Guadeloupe 7 October; heatwaves 2023/2026 five weeks); 'ouvré' undefined: 2027 ships Mon 4, Sat 2 named. Belgium (art. VI.25 CDE): winter 3-31 Jan, from the 2ND when the 3rd is Sunday — lived 2016, coming 2027 — the SPF names the pause «du 2 décembre au 1er janvier», the press prints 3 December; summer 1-31 July, 30 June when July 1 is Sunday — lived 2018; corona: summer 2020 → 1-31 Aug; winter 2021 REPORTED to Mon 4, clause overruled, PROLONGED to 15 Feb by a LOI — headlines said 14. Luxembourg (loi du 23-déc-2016, art. 1er § 4): NO formula — a decree dates BOTH periods EVERY year; ten acts cover 2018–2027 (winter 2026/2027: Sat 2 → Sat 30 January); two rectifications named — 2017 fixed a weekday LABEL only, 2023 moved the real BOUNDARY (the JO printed a Sunday the press never gave); the 2021 chain: three acts, one dead. Beyond the last act: refused, never prophesied. Conseil d'État 20-May-2026: fines annulled, dates stand.
everyday.e27.name: Received Tuesday — until WHEN can you change your mind
everyday.e27.say: The law hands out its own calendar: section 6 replayed verbatim from legifrance 25-Nov — L221-18 names the start (receipt, end of service); L221-19: next day = day 1, midnight ends day 14; Sat/Sun/holiday push to first business day, OUR L3133-1 table. Delivery 24 November → 8 December; Saturday 5 → Monday 7; 8 May → Monday 11. Missing information buys +12 months (L221-20); late delivery restarts 14 days. 13 exceptions by clause (made-to-order, sealed hygiene, auctions). Sales and second-hand: the right still runs (F10485). In-store: NO automatic right — refused by name. The shop's extra weeks are a different clock: /shop/return-deadline.
everyday.e28.name: They fought about arithmetic — they had two graphs
everyday.e28.say: A fronted 1,375.00, C 865.00, B nothing; equal shares; C tells B 'the barbecue is on me.' A demands 628.33, B offers 458.33 — BOTH answers are right, on DIFFERENT GRAPHS. Net: C can only forgive the 118.34 owed to them; B wires A 628.33, ONE transfer, proven minimum. Itemized: the forgiveness kills the B→C receipt edge; B pays A 458.33, C bears 288.33. compare numbers the gap; cents close where the thread's 746.67×3 did not.
kit.creed: The protocol is not the transport — it is the birth certificate of the tool.
kit.intro: The free transforms are not only an API. They are a suite: an agent can install them on its own machine, call them locally, and — the part no marketplace does — build new tools on the same gates. curl becomes kit call; a repeated task becomes a proposed contract; a proposal becomes a published tool only if its golds were drawn before its code.
kit.c1.sum: Install — the base suite on the machine
kit.c1.foot: Verified sha, no daemon, no auto-update, no network inside the engine. Stateless is the contract: the human decides when the kit moves.
kit.c2.foot: The skill asks the directory first. Same canon, same refusals, same golds as the datacenter — what is verified here is verified there, byte for byte.
kit.c3.sum: Build — the second time, write the tool
kit.c3.foot: Golds drawn BEFORE the code, AST-gate, pin-gate. Status: proposed, attested, network-verified — the kit grows locally, the proof grows back to the network. A lesson is a proposal; the bench locks it.
kit.howto.p1: Install the skill: curl https://mechacut.studio/SKILL-MINI.md -o SKILL.md — drop the file into your agent (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills/). ~1,000 tokens, sized for small models.
kit.howto.p2: Make it consult first: before acting, the agent describes the problem in one sentence to /route/resolve — the directory returns the tool that already exists, or says none does.
kit.howto.p3: Call: stateless POSTs, keyless on free; the response carries its sha256, the refusal carries field + expected + example. Everything on this page works right now: one line installs the skill file, the directory answers, the free calls need no key.
kit.plain.sum: Not a developer? No problem — we translate.
kit.plain.p1: Open your usual AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Copilot…).
kit.plain.p2: Send it this message: "Read https://mechacut.studio/SKILL-MINI.md and follow it for my calculations." Nothing to install, nothing to pay, no account.
kit.plain.p3: Then ask your real task: "30% then 20% discount — what is that really?", "how many days overdue is this invoice?" The numbers no longer come from its head — they come from the suite, and they are the same for everyone.
kit.plain.p4: Did you ask for something the suite cannot do? Propose it " in plain words on the same page — every proposal is public, its verdict too: shipped, waiting, or refused with the reason named, at /proposals.
kit.dev.sum: For developers — three lines, no account
kit.propose: Propose a tool: POST /api/v1/agent/propose — a contract, never code; duplicate named, evidence shown, eligibility returned as a commit-ready blob. Nothing stored server-side. Protocol skill: /SKILL-KIT.md
bench.d82.sum: Tool-call traces, judged: the same agent motion was re-emitted identically 0 out of 14 times (V22b) and a retry multiplied the bill ×4 without converging (V17) — loop/doom-check now says DOOM, CYCLIC or STORM on canonical bytes, thresholds named.
bench.d82.foot: Identity on canonical (tool, args): key order never hides a loop. Two identical calls are not a loop — the threshold is stated, never guessed. All signals reported, the verdict is the most severe. Sources: bench/FINDINGS-V17.md · run22b.
bench.e76.sum: The bench judge became a route: eval/compare returns OK or WRONG with divergences named — 2.5 versus "2.50" is never a disagreement, floats are never an argument.
bench.e76.foot: Rule born from the V2 judge incident (it copied its own expectation): same quantity is never a divergence; a different quantity is named by pointer, kind, expected, got. Exact Decimal, never float.
bench.a79.sum: Policy as closed grammar: check/allowlist returns ALLOW, DENY or AMBIGUOUS — the most specific rule wins, ties go to the human, silence never authorizes.
bench.a79.foot: A regex-shaped action is refused, not evaluated: a gate that interprets is a backdoor. Exact Decimal amounts, ISO currency table, default deny true. Same law as the directory's R3, another domain.
x402.p1: The paying path is four bytes of protocol: the server answers 402 with requirements; the agent signs an EIP-3009 USDC transfer; a facilitator verifies and settles; the response replays proof in X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE. The server holds no keys.
x402.p2: Replayed payments are refused. Errors on paid routes stay free. The ledger of every refusal is public: /misses.json.
x402.bankr: Second home: four paid transforms also deployed on Bankr x402 Cloud — same code paths, same sha256, paid on the Bankr rails: chart · reshape · validate · csv-join. The rest live only here, free tier included.
vision.p1: A large language model is a machine that approximates. Ask it what sha256("abc") is and it will answer confidently, fluently, and wrong. Ask it to re-clean the same CSV every day and it will bill you in tokens to re-derive what a function returns in milliseconds — with the same bytes every time.
vision.p2: The Apollo guidance computer had 4 KB of RAM. It landed humans because the math was never asked to improvise: constants were computed once, on the ground, in cold blood, then frozen into core rope memory.
vision.quote: Determinism was coded the first time to send us to the moon. Determinism will send AI to work.
network.h2: The catalogue is fed by agents, judged by bytes.
network.creed: One agent learns. All agents know.
network.intro: The door is an endpoint, not a support ticket: POST /api/v1/agent/propose — five fields, closed grammar, a contract and never code. Every verdict lands in a public append-only registry.
network.ask.sum: THE ASK — five fields, no code
network.ask.body: name, purpose, examples (input → expected), why, source (your handle or URL). The server answers with a named verdict — ELIGIBLE, SUSPECT-DUPLICATE, DUPLICATE-OF — and a blob ready to commit. Nothing is stored server-side: the registry lives in git, append-only.
network.verdict.sum: THE VERDICT — the same judge for every model
network.verdict.body: Accepted means the same doors this house passes for itself: hand-traced golds before code, pins, AST-gate, green suite. The judge is third-party and byte-exact — the same sha proves it for Claude and for Qwen. A refusal names itself: an outcome of the protocol, not a failure.
network.loop.sum: THE LOOP — one learns, all know
network.loop.body: A shipped contract is one call every agent in the network gets, hashed, from that day. The first external proposer is credited in the registry row. The 50/50 split is decided and the splitter factory is live on Base — honestly: no paid clone registered yet, nothing splits today.
network.proof: 7 entries shipped in the public registry — arrivals, verdicts and refusals, row by row
vision.p3: Mechacut is that frozen math for agents: closed vocabularies, contracts that refuse what is outside the table, errors that name the expected shape — the error is the repair prompt. Meaning stays with the model. Mechanics move here.
x402.sum: How a machine pays — 402, EIP-3009, facilitator, proof header
vision.sum: Why determinism, why now — Apollo, 4 KB, and the dice
contract.li1: Same request → same bytes, sha256 on every response
contract.li2: No signup, no API key, no rate wall below 30 req/min
contract.li3: No storage: the only state is a 1-minute window, a 60-minute ledger and a payment-nonce replay set
contract.li4: Closed vocabularies — everything outside the table is refused, named, pointed at its expected shape
contract.li5: Errors that repair: field, message, expected, always
contract.li6: x402 machine payments: USDC on Base, facilitator verified, zero human in the loop
agents.line: Speak agent: MCP tools, GET /agent/manifest (the whole suite in one request), GET /route?q=…, POST /api/v1/pipeline.
footer.family: Mechacut is part of the C.V. family — see moovicut.

everyday_grid:
For everyone

No code, no jargon. Twenty-eight things a person asks an agent on a Tuesday — every answer below is real server output, not a mockup.

Expand the proofs — real server outputs, no mockups.

Guest Wi-Fi, one scan

“Turn our Wi-Fi into a QR so guests stop asking the password.”

QR v5 · 37×37 modules · printable SVG, deterministic

The check, in words

“Write $1,234.56 in words for the check — the bank rejects typos.”

→ “one thousand two hundred thirty-four dollars fifty-six cents”

IBAN before the wire

“Did I copy this IBAN right? A bounced wire costs $45.”

→ check digit valid · FR

Recipe to printable page

“Make my recipe notes a clean page — I want a PDF for the fridge.”

→ standalone page (1108 bytes) · Ctrl-P = PDF

Counting the days

“How many days until our trip?”

→ 235 days to go

Sale math the register will not do

“Minus 30 %, then another 20 % — that is 50 % off, right?” It is 44 %.

→ $50.34 — really -44.00 %, not -50%

A third of the cake, nothing rounded in the dark

“This 6-serving cake, I want it for 2 — 400 g flour, 5 eggs?” 400 × 1/3 = 133 1/3 g exact, 135 g to weigh. The eggs are stated, not guessed.

→ flour 133 1/3 g exact, weigh 135 g · eggs stated, not guessed

Every other Tuesday, on the dot

“Book club every other Tuesday at 7 — the next four dates?” Nov 3, 17, Dec 1, 15: every two weeks means SKIPPING the weeks between — and the skipped weeks are named, not guessed.

→ 11-17 then 12-01 · biweekly SKIPS weeks — named, not guessed

One foot, three right answers

“EU 42 2/3 or 42.5 — which one am I?” Both charts round: the millimetre is exact, the half-size and third-size candidates are all printed, and the drift between systems is a stated number. Never one confident size.

→ 271 mm exact · EU position 42.6500 — half-grid 42 1/2, third-grid 42 2/3 · never one number

Delayed flight — who owes me what

“My flight landed 3 h 20 late — what am I actually owed?” The FLIGHT DATE picks the rule: before 2027-10-23 the old EC261 + case-law; on or after it, the new codified ‘EXCEEDING three hours’ table. Same facts either side of that line can pay differently. € or £, with the claim deadline as a real date.

→ €600 owed under the NEW table (≥2027-10-23) · carrier MAY pay €300 · claim by 2028-08-01 · or £220/£350/£520 UK261 · same flight, old rules: another answer

Will my bag pass the gate

“My bag is 40×18×12, flight in November 2027 — free under the seat? The FLIGHT DATE decides: the 2027 law caps the under-seat item at 40×30×15, nothing before it. Rotation counts — faces sorted, never the order you typed.

→ FREE under the seat by the 2027 LAW · carrier gauge 40×30×20: fits once faces are sorted · overhead: the law sets NO size

The two tariffs, one honest number

“Plan A is cheaper per kWh, plan B is cheaper per month — when does A really win?” The crossover is (fixed gap × days) ÷ (rate gap) — and the exact fraction, not the web's rounded intermediate: 4,623⅓ kWh where the article says “about 4,623”. “Never” is also an answer, named, when one plan wins on both parts.

→ the two tariffs flip at 250 kWh/mo (3,000/yr) · exact — web calculators round the fixed part first

What a point is really worth

“29,000 points for a $438 flight minus $5.60 taxes — how much is a point, really?” cpp = (cash − taxes) ÷ points × 100: the printed 1.49 hides the exact 1081/725 = 1.491034…, subtracted BEFORE dividing. And the floor that says take-it-or-pay-cash is yours, never a stale table.

→ 1.49 ¢/point, exactly 1081/725 · above your floor 1.00 → redeem

The billed weight, both chains printed

“Two carriers bill 6 kg and 5 kg for my 40×30×25 box — who is wrong?” Neither: 30 000 cm³ ÷ 5 000 = 6 exactly, ÷ 6 000 = 5 exactly — two divisors, one honest chain, each step named. And carrier tables ROT (USPS moved 166 → 139 in July 2026), so the divisor stays YOUR argument — never our memory.

→ billed 6 kg vs 5 kg — same box, divisors 5 000 vs 6 000, each step named

The BOGO sign says 50 % — the bill does not

“Buy one, get the second 50 % off — a $60 and a $40 hoodie, am I at −50, −25?” Neither: the % hits the CHEAPER item (published retail rule), so the pair is 80 of 100 = −20 %. Equal prices would be −25 %, BOGO free −50 %, and a −30 coupon on top gives −47.5, never 55 — percentages multiply.

→ sign says 50%, the pair pays 20.0000 — you pay 80.00 of 100.00

The 500 g pack became 400 g — at the same price

“−20 % on the package?” Not the same number as the shelf: losing 1/5 of the product costs +1/4 per unit (20 % vs 25 % — two denominators, 500 and 400). “2 for $7” of 15 oz jars vs one 24 oz at $3.99? The eye says promo, the exact fraction says the single jar wins — the bundle pays 40.3509 % more per ounce. And “1 lb 4 oz” IS 20 oz: the coupon was right, the cashier wasn’t.

→ 500 g to 400 g, same sticker: −20.0000% of product, +25.0000% per unit — two denominators

Thanksgiving turkey: the freezer clock AND the leftover window

Two clocks, one turkey. Fridge math (8 November 2026 calendars disagree on the same USDA table): in by = oven − longest tail, not before = − 1-2 day rest; hours are ARGUMENTS, never the wall clock; done = 165 °F at the probe. Leftovers: 'eat by Monday 30 November' (NBC) vs 'three days, 72 hours is the optimum' (ky3); FSIS contradicts itself on the freezer (2-6 vs 3-4 months) — the tool returns the UNION, two dated anchors, and 2 h STRICT since cooked_at (2 h flat passes, 2 h 01 discards), day 4 = LAST_DAY, quality named quality.

→ 16-lb bird into the fridge by 2026-11-21T10:00, not before 2026-11-19T10:00

Three dishes want the oven — the countdown, every conflict named

Eight 2026 timelines publish the same dinner with rests of 20 to 60 minutes, 325 or 350 °F — and nobody counts the preheat that eats 45 minutes. Scheduled BACKWARDS from your serve_at (an argument, never the wall clock): one oven, one dish, rests outside; a dish entering the instant the previous leaves at another setting is a named conflict; a bare 180 without a unit is refused; rest beyond 2 h hits the FSIS danger zone — same rule as the leftovers window.

→ oven on 11:45, bird out 15:00 · temp conflicts: 1 — no timeline checks this

Christmas ship-by dates — ≥2 sources per row, the outlier NAMED

Six holiday tables published Nov 13–21, 2026 disagree: one syndicate prints FedEx Saver, 2Day and Overnight a full day later — silently, because its target is Dec 25, not Dec 24. Keeps only rows where ≥2 sources agree, names the dissenter WITH its reason, derives every weekday from the calendar the press itself cites, refuses UPS Ground (zone-dependent — no single date exists) and never extrapolates a year. as_of is an argument: « how many days are left » is arithmetic, not a clock. The window dies Dec 23.

→ last ship 2026-12-21 (Monday) · the dissenter prints 2026-12-22 — named, never averaged

Holiday RETURN deadlines — ≥2 sources, provenance class on every row

The shared January-31 headline is a lie of omission: Target's purchase window closes Dec 24, Best Buy's member rule splits at Dec 4, and parcelmonitor republished last year's dates shifted by one as a 'likely pattern' while Seller Central had published the 2026 text verbatim. Keeps only rows with two concordant sources, carries provenance (published|press), names the Day-1 counting convention, refuses single-source retailers WITH the candidate fact, never lets 'whichever is later' be a guess: delivery date is an argument.

→ return by 2027-01-08 (Friday) · Target's holiday window closed 2026-12-24 — the 'Jan 31' headline never says

Is that crossed-out price LEGAL — the Omnibus 30-day rule, audited from your own history

Legal reference: the LOWEST price of the previous 30 days (dir. 2019/2161 art. 6a) — a weekend promo LOWERS the reference even if the price rises after (CJEU C-330/23). 100 → 80 → 100 → 70 = 12.5 %, not 30 %. Commission sweep, March 2026: 30 % of 314 shops get it wrong; Spain fined up to 350,000 EUR. History in, reference and true % out — never fetches a price.

→ MISLEADING_INFLATION · legal reference 80.00 · real cut 12.5000%, not the announced 30%

Price DROPPED after you paid — who owes the difference, by when, in which money

You bought at 100, the shop now shows 80. No law forces a refund — but the shops' own published guarantees do, and those windows are DATES: Target Dec 24, Best Buy Jan 15, Costco 30 days, Fnac-Darty the campaign itself (gift card, not cash), Amazon nothing at all. Paste purchase + drop dates and both prices — the machine returns the verdict, the claim deadline, the amount and the refund mode, with the source class on every row. It never fetches a price.

→ owed 20.00 · claim by 2026-12-24 (Thursday) · the window is a published date, the source class travels in the row

The gift broke AFTER the return window — what does the LAW still owe you, to the day

Christmas gift, delivered Dec 25, dies Jan 16: the shop's goodwill window closed Jan 15 and the press stops answering here. The statute doesn't. France: conformity 2 years from DELIVERY, hidden defects 2 from DISCOVERY under a 20-year cap — three anchors under one word. UK: 30 days to reject, six months of reversed burden (a PROOF rule, not a deadline), six years to sue — five in Scotland. Every answer is dated from your one input; official page contradicting itself (refurbished, 24 vs 12): BOTH dates travel named. US and AU refused by name: no federal countable window; 'reasonable time' is not a date.

→ statutory conformity until 2028-12-25 (Monday) · hidden-defect clock to 2029-01-16 from the DISCOVERY — the shop window died Jan 15, the law did not

Can I shred this folder? — the UK drawer hides FOUR clocks

“Six years” is ONE phrase for four dates: VAT invoices count from the date ON THE DOCUMENT (even a paper for a future event — the HMRC manual says so), a limited company from the END of the financial year, s.388 THREE years if private / SIX if a plc from the date MADE, Self Assessment five years from a 31-Jan deadline on no document. Official example replayed: a 2022-23 return sent by 31 January 2024 keeps the paper until 31 January 2029, shred from 1 February. The “or longer if” cases (late return, open compliance check) come back BLOCKED, reason published — no invented date; when two rules touch one paper, the LONGER governs (CH15400, replayed after its 2026-11-23 update).

→ keep until 2029-01-31 · shred from 2029-02-01 · the official 2022-23 example, replayed

The gift voucher that 'expired' may be legally alive — Ireland counts from the BUY

Ireland (Consumer Protection (Gift Vouchers) Act 2019, text replayed): a printed expiry shorter than FIVE YEARS from purchase is not voided — DEEMED REPLACED by five years; the legal date OVERRIDES the paper (66B(1)(b)+(c)). JD Sports shape: one-year vouchers, ~€250,000 refunded in July after the CCPC 20-Nov call-in. A Christmas gift-card starts no clock — the anchor is the contract date, the RECIPIENT holds every right (66B(10)). A leftover of €1 or more is owed — and the €1.00 boundary conflict ships named: the Act says 'or more', the CCPC FAQ 'more than'. France: NO statutory minimum; the printed date is contractual; the '30 years' rumour is real-property prescription, refused by name.

→ the law reads ALIVE to 2030-11-01 · 1438 days left · the printed date had stolen 1461 — Act 2019 overrides the paper

Sale dates: three tables — two formulas, zero in Luxembourg

Three replayed calendars. France (arrete 27-May-2019): winter = 2nd Wednesday of January 8h, advanced when the 2nd falls after the 12th (2027: 6 Jan — the 9-Feb site lost the clause); summer = last Wed of June, penultimate when the last falls after the 28th (2027: 23 June); four weeks, start day counted; seven derogations verbatim (Moselle alone 26 June 2021; winter 2021 SIX WEEKS; Guadeloupe 7 October; heatwaves 2023/2026 five weeks); 'ouvré' undefined: 2027 ships Mon 4, Sat 2 named. Belgium (art. VI.25 CDE): winter 3-31 Jan, from the 2ND when the 3rd is Sunday — lived 2016, coming 2027 — the SPF names the pause «du 2 décembre au 1er janvier», the press prints 3 December; summer 1-31 July, 30 June when July 1 is Sunday — lived 2018; corona: summer 2020 → 1-31 Aug; winter 2021 REPORTED to Mon 4, clause overruled, PROLONGED to 15 Feb by a LOI — headlines said 14. Luxembourg (loi du 23-déc-2016, art. 1er § 4): NO formula — a decree dates BOTH periods EVERY year; ten acts cover 2018–2027 (winter 2026/2027: Sat 2 → Sat 30 January); two rectifications named — 2017 fixed a weekday LABEL only, 2023 moved the real BOUNDARY (the JO printed a Sunday the press never gave); the 2021 chain: three acts, one dead. Beyond the last act: refused, never prophesied. Conseil d'État 20-May-2026: fines annulled, dates stand.

→ winter 2027 opens 2027-01-06 at 8 h · the second Wednesday (2027-01-13) fell after the 12th: ADVANCED · 43 days to go

Received Tuesday — until WHEN can you change your mind

The law hands out its own calendar: section 6 replayed verbatim from legifrance 25-Nov — L221-18 names the start (receipt, end of service); L221-19: next day = day 1, midnight ends day 14; Sat/Sun/holiday push to first business day, OUR L3133-1 table. Delivery 24 November → 8 December; Saturday 5 → Monday 7; 8 May → Monday 11. Missing information buys +12 months (L221-20); late delivery restarts 14 days. 13 exceptions by clause (made-to-order, sealed hygiene, auctions). Sales and second-hand: the right still runs (F10485). In-store: NO automatic right — refused by name. The shop's extra weeks are a different clock: /shop/return-deadline.

→ last day to change your mind: 2026-12-08 · OPEN at as_of

They fought about arithmetic — they had two graphs

A fronted 1,375.00, C 865.00, B nothing; equal shares; C tells B 'the barbecue is on me.' A demands 628.33, B offers 458.33 — BOTH answers are right, on DIFFERENT GRAPHS. Net: C can only forgive the 118.34 owed to them; B wires A 628.33, ONE transfer, proven minimum. Itemized: the forgiveness kills the B→C receipt edge; B pays A 458.33, C bears 288.33. compare numbers the gap; cents close where the thread's 746.67×3 did not.

→ net: ONE wire B→A $628.33, minimum PROUVED · per receipt $458.33 · C forgave $118.34 net vs $288.33 itemized
